title: NaN-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for reproducing and triaging NaN/quality regressions when switching model serving to low-precision paths (INT8 / FP8 / BF16).

Background:
- Observed intermittent NaNs in streaming generation on prod-dedicated nodes after enabling FP8 kernels (opt-level fast-kernel).
- Same model in FP32 runs cleanly. BF16 mostly fine but small probability of instability on some prompts. INT8 path shows large perplexity regressions on rare sequences (not always NaN).
- Hypothesis: quantization scale overflow in attention softmax or GEMM kernel under long-prefix KV cache + continuous batching. Could be per-tensor vs per-channel scale mismatch, or mis-handling of fp8 exponent bias between kernels.

Repro steps tried so far (commands + envs):
1) baseline FP32 (no autocast) - stable
   $ OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m experiments.run_infer --model checkpoint/latest --dtype fp32 --batch-size 1 --prompt-file tests/suspicious-prompts.txt

2) BF16 (autocast) - mostly stable, occasional token-score spike (not NaN)
   $ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m experiments.run_infer --model checkpoint/latest --dtype bf16 --batch-size 4 --autocast True

3) FP8 fast kernels (enabled) - reproduced NaN within ~30-120s on a prompt set
   $ FI_PRECISION=fp8 FI_KERNEL=fast OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m experiments.run_infer --model checkpoint/latest --dtype fp8 --cache-enabled True --continuous-batch 1
   - log snippet: "Step 87: loss=nan, logits[0,3]=nan, attention_scores contains nan at row 512"

4) INT8 quantized weights + dynamic activation quant (runtime) - no NaN but huge quality drop for some prompts
   $ ./scripts/serve_quant.sh --model quantized/int8/checkpoint --act-quant dynamic --batch 8

What I dumped / inspected:
- saved activations before attention softmax (float32 cast) for failing step -> found extremely large values (~1e8) in attention logits for a small subset of tokens -> implies scale blowup upstream.
- weight histograms for linear layers: some channels have long tails; per-channel quantization reduces MSE there but still hit extremes.
- calibration stats from calibration run: min/max ranges very wide for certain layers using per-tensor symmetric quant; suspect need for outlier clipping.
- FP8 metadata in kernel header (exponent bias) matched our runtime at compile-time? Confirmed matching major version but not minor.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Activation scale blowup due to mixed-precision accumulation mismatch (FP8 kernel accumulates into FP16/FP32?). Some kernels expect accumulation in FP32; ours uses FP16 for perf -> overflow -> NaN.
2) Incorrect exponent bias or EVEX packing mismatch between compiled FP8 kernels and runtime conversion code. Small shift causes values to saturate.
3) KV cache indexing bug under continuous batching causes reading uninitialized memory which becomes NaN, which then propagates via softmax and throws off quant scales.
4) Calibration pipeline used rep dataset that's missing tokens that trigger rare high-attention scores -> dynamic quant sees unseen outliers and produces large scales.

Experiments to run next (TODO):
- [ ] Rebuild FP8 kernels forcing accumulation to FP32 (compile flag FORCE_ACCUM_FP32=1) and run 1000-step loop on failing prompt. Compare with current build.
- [ ] Insert asserts/guards in attention kernel to clamp logits to +/-1e4 before softmax as a canary (should never be needed). Test whether NaNs vanish (helps isolate overflow vs memory corruption).
- [ ] Run with ASan/MemorySanitizer on CPU path to detect reads of uninitialized memory for KV cache indexing patterns (use smaller model for speed).
- [ ] Collect per-layer scale history (tensor of scales at each inference step) to see if scale drifts before NaN. Persist to /tmp/quant-scales-runid.npz (but currently store as JSON lines for readability).
- [ ] Try per-channel activation quantization for top-k linear layers (experiment config: act-quant=per-channel) and compare calibration min/max kurtosis.
- [ ] Re-run calibration with extended rep set that includes long prefix contexts and some adversarial prompts from customer logs.

Quick checks already done:
- toggled torch.backends.cudnn.enabled True/False -> no difference
- disabled fused-kernel optimizations in compile -> FP8 still produced NaN but later (longer time to fail)
- set PYTORCH_JIT=0 -> no change
- added torch.cuda.synchronize() between KV writes/reads -> slight improvement but not full fix

Logs and error snippets (copied raw):
- "epoch: 0 step: 12821 loss: nan, logit[12]=-inf, grad_norm=nan, attention_sum=inf"
- core dump backtrace shows GEMM kernel (optimized_gemm_fp8.cu) -> reduce_sum -> softmax -> nans propagate
- kernel trace: "fp8_pack: exponent=7, mantissa_trunc=2, scale=2.3e-6 -> packed_val=127 -> overflow when dequant"

Notes on quant config options that matter here:
- per-tensor symmetric vs per-channel: per-channel helps weights with heavy tails but not activations unless we instrument dynamic per-channel activation observers (costly).
- calibration method: minmax vs percentile (99.9) vs KL-divergence-based. For attention logits, percentile clipping at 99.995 seemed to reduce extreme logits but can bias distribution and hurt rare-case QA accuracy.
- accumulation dtype: change from fp16 to fp32 increases stability but doubles bandwidth and reduces throughput. Need to quantify SLO impact.

Immediate mitigations suggested for prod: (short term)
- disable FP8 fast-kernel rollout for dedicated-prod nodes until kernel rebuild and per-layer scale logging are in place.
- enable detection guard: treat NaN logits as trigger to fallback to FP32 model on that request (graceful degrade). Implemented as policy in router: if token_score is nan -> reroute to fp32 endpoint and log request id.

Questions for kernel team (to raise in sync):
- Do FP8 kernels assume accumulation in FP32? Where is that documented in our kernel API?
- Any known ABI changes in latest cuda primitives that could break exponent packing?
- Can we get a reproducible unit test that deterministically triggers NaN under small model locally?

Notes-to-self (random):
- check PR #1342 for an accidental change to fp8_pack/unpack semantics.
- follow up with Priya on telemetry: add per-token NaN counters in request logs (low overhead counter metric).
- document safe rollout checklist for low-precision kernels (calibration coverage, fallback, telemetry).

Mini-experiment plan (short):
1) Build fast-kernel with FORCE_ACCUM_FP32=1, run 50k tokens across 10 prompts that historically failed. Measure NaN count, latency, p99.
2) If zeros NaN: bisect by toggling single-layer accum->fp16 to find problematic layer.
3) If still NaN: run ASan/Memcheck to rule out memory bug.

References / quick links embedded:
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342
- perf config used for failing run: git@github.com:redwood-inference/configs.git:quant/fp8-fast.yaml
- jira issue: JIRA-INF-9876

End-of-note.

(Will iterate as I run the experiments. Keep short-term fixes in router until root cause confirmed.)
